leads.title: Montana Senate Bill 458 (2023) - biological definition of 'sex'
leads.documents: Codifies immutable male-female binary determined at birth; basis for state-level non-recognition of transgender status relevant to legal status and equal protection.
leads.detail: Signed May 2023 by Gov. Greg Gianforte; struck down Feb 2025 by District Judge Leslie Halligan as violating equal protection clauses of Constitution of Montana. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Montana Senate Bill 437 (2026) - definitions of gender, male, female, man, woman, mother, father
leads.documents: Mandates 'gender' as synonym for 'sex', prohibits 'gender identity' as substitute; criticized as erasing transgender, intersex, two-spirit recognition from state law.
leads.detail: Signed March 2026; passed in 2025 session but delayed by SB 458 litigation; plaintiffs requested addition to ongoing litigation April 2026 as fundamentally identical to SB 458. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana Senate Bill 99 (2023) - prohibition on gender-affirming care for trans minors
leads.documents: Most comprehensive state ban on gender-affirming care for minors; litigation history shows current enforceability and courts' view of discrimination and privacy rights.
leads.detail: Signed April 28, 2023 by Gov. Gianforte; preliminarily enjoined Sept 27, 2023 by District Judge Jason Marks citing Bostock v. Clayton County; injunction upheld Dec 11, 2024 by Montana Supreme Court with concurrence by Justice Laurie McKinnon on suspect class; permanently struck down May 14, 2025 by Judge Marks. ACLU of Montana and Lambda Legal filed suit. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana birth certificate and driver's license gender-marker restrictions and injunctions
leads.documents: Documents ability of trans visitors/residents to update ID documents; enforcement status of bans on changes absent data-entry error, DNA test, or surgery/court order.
leads.detail: Sept 9, 2022 DPHHS rule banning updates, blocked Sept 15, 2022; Feb 22, 2023 bill prohibiting changes on all IDs signed May 19, 2023; enjoined Dec 2024 by District Judge Mike Menahan; preliminary block Dec 16, 2024 extended to trial citing sex discrimination; upheld April 15, 2026 by Montana Supreme Court, Justice Laurie McKinnon on dignity. Prior rules: surgery required until Dec 2017, then affidavit + Gender Designation Form + court order; April 2021 surgical-procedure requirement blocked April 2022 for vagueness, followed by May 2022 emergency rule. ACLU sued July 2021. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana House Bill 121 (2025) - sex-segregated bathrooms, locker rooms, sleeping areas in publicly-funded facilities
leads.documents: Direct safety/access risk for trans visitors using public facilities; shows enforcement attempt and judicial check.
leads.detail: Passed Feb 2025; ACLU of Montana sued; temporary restraining order April 2, 2025 by District Court Judge Shane Vannatta ruling bill 'motivated by animus' with no evidence advancing women's safety/privacy. Also cites failed 2018 Montana Family Foundation ballot initiative and Dec 3, 2024 House vote down of Capitol bathroom ban affecting Rep. Zooey Zephyr. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana House Bill 359 (2023) - restriction on sexually oriented/obscene performances and drag story hours
leads.documents: Criminalization risk around drag/trans expression in public spaces where minors may be present and in publicly-funded schools/libraries.
leads.detail: Passed May 2023 along party lines; led to cancellation of Butte-Silver Bow library reading by transgender woman; temporarily restrained July 2023 prior to Big Sky Pride by District Court Judge Brian Morris as 'vague and overbroad' with risk of disproportionate enforcement against trans, Two-Spirit, gender nonconforming people; extended Oct 2024. Follow-on HB 675 defeated March 2025 with 13 Republicans joining Democrats. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana House Bill 819 (May 2025) - government flag 'neutrality' law
leads.documents: Prohibits official display of flags representing sexual orientation, gender, political ideology; interpreted to ban Pride flags by governments/schools; Missoula rainbow-flag municipal-flag workaround.
leads.detail: Defines flag as physical/digital installation on flagpole, building, wall, vehicle, structure; exempts governmental, territorial, school, historical (e.g., Gadsden), law enforcement flags. No URL visible.

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, 590 U.S. (June 15, 2020) - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Establishes federal Title VII protection against workplace discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity as sex discrimination, applicable in Montana despite lack of state statute.
leads.detail: Consolidated with Altitude Express v. Zarda and R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes v. EEOC; cited by Montana courts in SB 99 case. Complements Montana Executive Orders: 2000 Gov. Marc Racicot personnel rules, Nov 2008 Gov. Brian Schweitzer EO 41-2008, Jan 2016 Gov. Steve Bullock expansion to gender identity and contractors. No URL visible.

leads.title: Montana hate-crime statutes gap and Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (2009)
leads.documents: Documents that Montana hate-crime law does not include sexual orientation or gender identity; federal prosecution avenue only, critical for safety dossier on bias-violence recourse.
leads.detail: Federal Act signed Oct 2009 by President Barack Obama allows federal prosecution for SOGI-based hate crimes. No URL visible.

leads.title: Censure and barring of Rep. Zooey Zephyr (April 2023) - documented enforcement incident
leads.documents: Incident showing state-house enforcement against openly trans lawmaker after opposition to SB 99; protest policing, 7 arrests, exclusion from floor until adjournment.
leads.detail: April 18, 2023 remarks on SB 99 ('tantamount to torture,' 'blood on your hands'); Montana Freedom Caucus misgendering statement; Speaker Matt Regier denied speaking; April 24 rally ~100 people, gallery chant 'let her speak,' riot police clearance, 7 arrested and released without bail; April 26 House vote 68-32 along party lines to bar from floor, gallery, antechamber. No URL visible.
